_doc: How each kind of planet is drawn in the battle (src/Game/View/PlanetLooks.cs, read into src/Game/View/planet.gdshader and planet_atmosphere.gdshader; owner, 2026-11-08: "In game Planets: pull in planets from godot-sandbox and falchion"). One look per PlanetDef.Kinds. Ported from Falchion's PLANET_LOOKS (RubenTipparach/falchion 5d128af8, src/content/planetLooks.ts): surface is rocky (noise terrain with seas, caps, craters and canyons), gas (warped bands and a storm) or lava (rocky with glowing cracks); palette is deep water, shallow water, lowland, highland for rocky and lava worlds, three bands and the storm for gas; sea is the terrain height (-1 to 1) below which it is liquid (below -1: none); ice_lat the latitude share (0 to 1) where the caps begin (above 1: none); clouds the cover, 0 to 1; detail the noise frequency (more, smaller continents); craters and canyons the landforms; glow the colour of lava and volcanoes; city_glow and cities the night side's lights and how much land they cover (0 to 1); volcanoes adds cones with lit calderas. The atmosphere shell is godot-sandbox's single scattering shell (RubenTipparach/godot-sandbox 63f463f7, resources/shaders/comic_atmosphere_shell.gdshader): atmosphere its tint, atmosphere_strength how strongly it scatters (0: no shell), atmosphere_height its top as a share of the radius above the ground. Layers over the ground (src/Game/View/PlanetBody.cs; owner, 2026-11-09: "We need some really good in game planet shaders ... Make a few different planet types ... gas giants with rings"; the planet-shaders skill, after godot-sandbox's stack of shells): cloud_layer is godot-sandbox's domed, lit weather (planet_clouds.gdshader; cover 0 to 1, scale its cloud systems round the world, lit and base the colours of thick and thin cloud, opacity), which turns the ground's painted clouds off; crater_cover is the share of godot-sandbox's crater lattice stamped (planet_craters.gdshader, 0 to 1); rings are a flat ring system (planet_rings.gdshader; inner and outer edges in the planet's radii, color_in and color_out, opacity) whose shadow a gas giant's tops take; tilt_deg leans the axis (degrees). A gas surface is planet_gas.gdshader, its flow in gas: bands (belt and zone pairs), turbulence (how torn their edges are), storm_lat (the great storm's latitude as a sine), storm_size (radians) and ovals (how many small white ovals, 0 to 1); its palette is zones, belts, the brightest bands and the storm.
